item.title: Latto Celebrates Angel Reese Win At Arena That Moved Her Show
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Latto joined Angel Reese after Atlanta's first WNBA Finals win, days before her rescheduled Chase Center date with Doja Cat.
item.content:encoded:
Latto joined Angel Reese at Chase Center after the Atlanta Dream’s first WNBA Finals win on October 19. The rapper had been due to play that same arena with Doja Cat that night.

The WNBA shared a clip of the pair posing near the court after Atlanta beat the Golden State Valkyries 79-65. Latto wore a red cap and black jacket as Reese put an arm around her for photos.

“THEY’RE SO ATL,” the league wrote. It posted the video at 10:50 P.M. Eastern on October 19, after the Dream tied the title series at one game each.

Reese scored 30 points and grabbed 16 rebounds in the win. Atlanta had lost all 10 of its prior Finals games. The Dream had been swept in three past trips, then lost Saturday’s opener to Golden State.

Latto’s own date at the arena had changed before the game. Chase Center’s event page named her as Doja Cat’s special guest for the “Tour Ma Vie World Tour.” It said Golden State’s run to the Finals moved their show from October 19 to October 25. Tickets stayed valid for the new date.

Latto and Reese had ties long before the Finals. Reese appeared in the 2023 video for “Put It On Da Floor Again,” Latto’s song with Cardi B. Reese was still at LSU then, and Cardi’s verse referred to the school.

Latto also went to Reese’s WNBA debut in May 2024, when the Chicago Sky faced the Dallas Wings at College Park Center in Arlington, Texas. In a courtside interview, Latto said she had come to watch Reese. She spoke up for women as more fans tuned in to the league.

“I’m here for the girl power period. Let’s go Angel Reese,” Latto said at the time.

This time, Reese played for Atlanta with a title at stake. Her team bounced back from a 68-64 loss in Game 1 and left the Bay Area with a split. Both clubs still sought their first league title.

The next two games were set for State Farm Arena in Atlanta. Game 3 was scheduled for October 21 at 8 P.M. Eastern. Latto and Doja Cat’s Chase Center show was listed for October 25.

item.title: Lil Jon Says Memoir Led To Discovery About His Biological Father
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Lil Jon said his memoir led to a family discovery. He also returned to the finished book after his son Nathan's death.
item.content:encoded:
Lil Jon said he learned the man who raised him was not his biological father while writing his memoir, “I Only Shout So You Can Hear Me.” The book reaches readers on October 20.

In his ABC News interview, Lil Jon said that he had long kept his personal life private. His team urged him to tell his story, and he chose to share what he learned.

“I could have left that out,” he said.

In an interview with People, Lil Jon said he learned this after a cousin took a DNA test. His cousin shared the results, and the two did not match as expected. The cousin assured him they were still family.

Lil Jon said both his biological father and Willie, the man who raised him, had died, as had his mother, Carrie. That left him with questions he could not put to them.

“Neither one of my fathers are here anymore, nor my mother, so I can’t get answers,” he told People.

The memoir took another turn after the death of Lil Jon’s son, Nathan Smith. Lil Jon told ABC News the book was already done when he went back and wrote an epilogue about his loss. He hoped sharing what he went through would help someone facing the same grief.

Nathan, known in music as DJ Young Slade, was 27 when his body was found in a pond in Milton, Georgia, on February 6. He worked as an artist, producer and engineer and had followed his father’s path into music.

Lil Jon said fans of his meditation albums had told him the records helped them sleep and deal with grief. He hoped sharing his own loss could help people in the same way.

His 2024 album “Total Meditation” includes “Coping With Grief.” Lil Jon made that project with Kabir Sehgal.

The publisher lists the memoir at 304 pages, written with Paul Cantor. Its account of family loss sits alongside Lil Jon’s years in Atlanta’s music scene, the rise of crunk, burnout and his return to DJing.

Atria/Black Privilege Publishing releases the book in the United States on October 20.

item.title: Rick Ross’ Son Reports Pistol-Whipping & Death Threat
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Rick Ross' son reported a pistol-whipping and death threat near his Daytona Beach college, according to a WFTV report.
item.content:encoded:
Rick Ross‘ son told police a man hit him in the head with a gun after a death threat that brought up his famous dad.

William Roberts III said the attack took place near his college in Daytona Beach on October 11. WFTV shared his account in an October 20 report based on police records.

Roberts said he was on a sidewalk with a woman when a driver pulled up and aimed a gun at him.

“I don’t care who your daddy is, I’ll kill you right here,” the man said, per the account WFTV cited.

Roberts said the man then struck him with the gun. Police noted slight swelling on the right side of his head, but he said he did not need medical care.

He later picked a suspect out of a photo lineup. Police checked city cameras but found no video of the attack.

Roberts plays football at Bethune-Cookman University. He is the son of Rick Ross and Tia Kemp, but his path to the school was built on years of work on the field.

The school announced his signing in 2024. He had played at St. Thomas Aquinas in Fort Lauderdale and helped his team win four state titles in four years.

In a 2024 profile, the Daytona Beach News-Journal asked Roberts what it was like to grow up with a star for a dad. He said that life in the spotlight had become normal to him, though he knew most kids did not share that life.

His ties to coach Raymond Woodie Jr. helped draw him to the school, even with offers from larger football programs. He also liked that he could stay in Florida.

“It just felt like home,” Roberts said at the time.

Once there, his goal was to help the team win. He told the paper he did not mind where coaches put him, as long as he could do his part. His choice came down to the bond he felt with the coach and the people in the program.

WFTV placed the alleged attack at McLeod Avenue and Weaver Street. Its report gave no motive or word of an arrest.

item.title: Wale Salutes Angel Reese & Gabby Williams On WNBA Finals Anthem
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Wale's Finals track salutes Angel Reese and Gabby Williams as the Dream and Valkyries battle for their first WNBA title.
item.content:encoded:
Wale gave Angel Reese and Gabby Williams their own shoutouts on “WYFL,” a new anthem for the 2026 WNBA Finals.

The league rolled out the track on Monday, October 19, as the Atlanta Dream and Golden State Valkyries chased their first titles. Wale released the full song on his own YouTube channel, which lists the WNBA as a collaborator.

The title stands for “Who You Feeling Like?” Wale names stars on both sides of the court in the song, which arrived before Game 2 at San Francisco’s Chase Center.

On X, the league said Wale “made this one for the W” as it introduced the record.

Reese, the league’s Defensive Player of the Year, is in her first season with Atlanta. She led the WNBA in rebounds during the regular season. Williams finished second in the award vote and became Golden State’s first All-Star starter this year. She also scored 26 points in the Valkyries’ 68-64 win in Game 1. Both teams reached the Finals with semifinal sweeps.

Atlanta then beat Golden State 79-65 in Game 2, tying the series at one game each. The win gave the Dream their first Finals victory after three past trips to the title round.

Wale has a long history of making music part of the live sports experience. The Wizards named him their creative liaison in 2014. He later made a team-themed song for the Sacramento Kings’ game intro in 2019.

His sports work also reached the soccer field this year. He played halftime at D.C. United’s March 7 match against Inter Miami in Baltimore. That game drew 72,026 fans, a club record.

Bay Area rappers have also had a role in this Finals. Too $hort was booked to handle the pregame drum for Game 2, with LaRussell on the halftime lineup. Larry June played halftime at the series opener.

Golden State reached the Finals in just its second season. Atlanta made it back for the first time since 2013. The title round uses a best-of-seven format.

The series moves to Atlanta for Game 3 on Wednesday, October 21. Tipoff is set for 8 P.M. Eastern at State Farm Arena, with the game on USA Network, CNBC and Peacock.

item.title: AKA Murder Trial: Airport Footage Draws Identity Challenge
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Airport footage drew a defense challenge in AKA's murder trial as lawyers weighed who could be identified in the video.
item.content:encoded:
AKA‘s murder trial turned to airport video Monday as the defense challenged whether a man seen following him could be identified.

The Durban High Court saw the video on October 19. It showed AKA moving through King Shaka International Airport on the day he was killed, including a stop at a car-rental counter.

Eyewitness News reported that the state did not ask the airport’s analyst to identify the man. The outlet said he resembled defendant Mziwethemba Gwabeni, but that description did not come from an identification by the witness.

Gwabeni’s lawyer, William Nicholson, argued that the man could not be identified and that the witness lacked the ability to do so.

The footage showed a man near the rental counter’s entrance while AKA was inside. When the rapper left, the man seemed to follow him toward the parking lot.

AKA wore a purple jacket, while the man wore shorts and appeared to speak on a phone. He walked past the rental area before turning back and looking toward parked cars.

The airport analyst said the system could not export footage for use on other devices, though he could make still images and had given those to the state.

“When viewing this footage, you are viewing the original and not the copy,” he told the court, The Star reported.

Nicholson also questioned whether the witness was breaching work rules by testifying. The analyst said the airport had agreed to show the video after an officer working on the case asked for it. He did not know if they had been summoned to court.

The state had told a bail court that Gwabeni followed AKA at the airport. Monday’s session brought the footage itself before the trial court, where the defense challenged what it could establish.

AKA, born Kiernan Forbes, and his friend Tebello “Tibz” Motsoane were shot dead on Durban’s Florida Road on February 10, 2023. All seven men pleaded not guilty in the case, which includes murder, conspiracy, attempted-murder and gun charges.

The airport evidence followed last week’s accounts of the shooting’s aftermath. The current trial block runs through November 6, and the analyst was due to return to the stand Tuesday, October 20.

item.title: BloodHound Q50 Autopsy Reveals Five Gunshot Wounds In Unsolved Killing
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: BloodHound Q50's new autopsy details added to the record of his fatal Chicago ambush, with no arrests reported in the case.
item.content:encoded:
BloodHound Q50 was shot five times when gunmen killed him in Chicago last month. The details came from a new report on his autopsy.

The findings came from Cook County’s medical examiner, the Chicago Sun-Times reported. About 50 spent casings from rifles and 9 mm handguns were found at the BP station in Fuller Park, the paper reported.

Q50, whose real name was Mikquale T. Cooper, was 22 when he died in the September 13 attack. Police said two cars pulled up while he sat in a vehicle outside the gas station. Several people got out and began to shoot, FOX 32 reported at the time. Paramedics treated him at the scene.

The station was at 4248 S. Wentworth Avenue. Police placed the attack just before 4 A.M. The Sun-Times’ new account said six gunmen opened fire. His girlfriend told police she fled and hid in a stranger’s car, records in the autopsy file showed.

FOX 32 spoke to a woman who said she had been there. She said she saw the men approach and tried to warn Q50, then ran when the shots began. The station did not name her.

At the time, police urged people who knew what had happened to come forward. Area One detectives took on the case.

The killing cut short a rap career that had begun in 2023. “Big 3” and “Coffin” helped build his name. He signed with Signal Records by the end of 2024, FOX 32 reported. He had also performed at Rolling Loud in May.

His funeral in Merrillville, held September 25, drew several police forces. They kept watch on the route down Taft Street to Calumet Park Cemetery. Assistant Chief Matt Vasel said they took those steps to keep the service on a main road safe.

The new Sun-Times report cited a police alert about the risk of revenge attacks after the funeral. It also noted that Naseem D. Stevens was shot dead that day. His car had a “funeral” sticker. Police records called a link between the deaths uncertain, not confirmed.

No arrests in Q50’s case had been reported in the paper’s latest account.

item.title: Nicki Minaj Named Trump’s New Press Secretary In Jimmy Fallon Spoof
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Nicki Minaj's Trump ties became a late-night punchline as Jimmy Fallon used edited footage for a fake White House hire.
item.content:encoded:
Nicki Minaj got a fake White House job when Jimmy Fallon made her the punchline of a skit about President Donald Trump’s search for a new press secretary.

The gag aired on “The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon” on Monday (October 19). The show used a clip of Trump saying the rap star’s name as if he had just hired her.

AOL’s account of the sketch said that Fallon staged a mock chat with Katie Zacharia. The show cut clips from her first press briefing into answers to his questions.

He asked how long she had hoped to hold the job. The reply was “A very long time.” Asked how long she had lasted, the next clip gave him “Several days.”

The sketch also used a law license question for a gag. A clip supplied “From Amazon” as the answer to where she got her license.

At the end, Fallon said Trump was naming his new hire. The show cut to the president saying, “Nicki Minaj.”

Minaj’s real ties to Trump had already brought her to his small-business contest and to Fox News. AllHipHop reported in September that she went on “The Ingraham Angle” with Small Business Administration chief Kelly Loeffler.

The pair spoke about the Million Dollar Pitch Competition. Minaj had joined Grant Cardone and Airbnb co-founder Joe Gebbia as judges. The contest offered $1 million to small-business owners.

“I am honored to have the opportunity to work with this administration and to work with President Trump,” she said on the show.

She told Laura Ingraham that Trump made her feel heard. She also said she would not make excuses for her support of him.

Later that month, she urged young people to vote for Republicans on “My View with Lara Trump.” She told them to take part in local races as well as votes for president. Her plea stressed that they had a stake in how the country was run.

Fallon’s joke followed Zacharia’s October 16 exit after five days in the role. BBC’s “Global News Podcast” said she left as critics questioned her first briefing and her work in law.

item.title: Blueface Reportedly Arrested After Santa Clarita Gun Scare
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Blueface faced another police encounter while streaming after a gun report sent deputies to a Santa Clarita business.
item.content:encoded:
Blueface faced a new police run-in while live on Kick after a gun scare at a Santa Clarita business. Police checked the claim and found no man with a gun at the scene.

TMZ, citing a sheriff’s spokesperson, reported Blueface’s arrest and booking after he allegedly ignored commands.

The October 19 call brought police to a business on Magic Mountain Parkway, according to KTLA. The local sheriff’s watch commander told the station that the first report was about a man with a gun.

The watch commander described a chaotic scene as deputies answered what they treated as an emergency call.

Deputies held one person who did not obey their commands, the watch commander said. They suspected that person had delayed or blocked their work, a misdemeanor.

KTLA named Blueface as the person detained based on a post from local outlet What’s Up SCV. KTLA noted that the watch commander could not confirm the person’s name.

The run-in follows a string of false calls that have brought police to Blueface’s home and a local seafood spot. In two earlier cases, police held him while they checked a gun report, then let him go when they found no crime.

On August 23, deputies went to King of Crab on Bouquet Canyon Road after a report of a shooting. Sgt. Josh Nemeth told City News Service that Blueface had been detained and then released.

“Deputies responded, completed an investigation and determined no crime occurred at the location,” Nemeth said.

A July 21 call sent police to his Canyon Country home while he was live on Kick. Sheriff’s spokesperson Shirley Miller said a search found no shooting or sign of a crime.

More recently, two calls on September 30 sent crews back to his home. One alleged harm to a child. The other claimed a medical crisis. Crews found no medical emergency during the second visit.

AllHipHop also reported a police visit earlier this month, though authorities had not confirmed that call was deliberately false.

The latest reports did not identify who placed Monday’s call or say whether police had linked it to the earlier incidents.

item.title: Mariah Carey Wins Dismissal As Judge Rejects Brother’s Film-Loss Claim
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Mariah Carey won dismissal of her brother's memoir suit after a judge found gaps in his $1.5 million-plus film-loss claim.
item.content:encoded:
Mariah Carey won dismissal of her brother’s memoir suit after a judge found key gaps in his claims. That includes his claim of more than $1.5 million in lost film work.

Judge Leslie A. Stroth threw out Morgan Carey’s latest complaint. The 11-page decision was filed Monday, October 19. The order was signed October 9. It concerns his claims over her 2020 book, “The Meaning of Mariah Carey.”

Morgan sued in March 2021, saying parts of the book harmed his reputation and cost him work. The latest ruling faults his claims about Mariah’s state of mind. It also finds gaps in his claim of lost film work.

The case falls under New York’s anti-SLAPP law. It protects speech on matters of public interest. Morgan had to meet the “actual malice” test. He had to plead facts showing Mariah knew a statement was false or acted with reckless disregard for the truth.

“Notably, Plaintiff fails to provide any proof that Defendant made such statements with knowledge of their falsity or with reckless disregard for the truth,” Judge Stroth wrote.

The judge also found that claims of ill will toward her brother did not meet that test. Morgan had argued that Mariah put book sales ahead of checking her sources. The court found his claims fell short.

The film dispute gave the judge a second reason to reject parts of his case.

Morgan said he and his wife wrote a script called “Devil’s Hollow.” He claimed a producer in Italy backed a film franchise. The plan called for a movie, a prequel, a sequel and a spinoff series. He said the producer pulled out after learning about the memoir. A deal was still being drafted, in Morgan’s account.

He claimed more than $1.5 million in losses from the canceled project and the wider franchise. But he still hadn’t laid out the deal’s terms or an exact sum for his loss, the judge found.

Judge Stroth wrote: “However, Plaintiff still fails to detail the terms of the agreement and fails to quantify the specific amount of damages suffered beyond the general, ‘in excess of $1.5 million.'”

The order directs court clerks to enter judgment. It also denied Morgan’s bid to lift a pause on discovery as moot.

Mariah’s lawyer, John Rosenberg, told Billboard she welcomed the ruling. He said she views it as a win for authors who speak on matters of public concern.

Morgan’s lawyer, Richard Altman, told the outlet he plans to appeal. He said the decision conflicts with earlier rulings in the case.

item.title: D4vd Murder Trial Faces Major Delays As Rumors Swirl About Missing Millions
item.dc:creator: Houston Williams
item.description: D4vd's murder case takes another turn as questions about his missing millions, new public defenders and a possible 2027 trial delay intensify.
item.content:encoded:
D4vd may have earned millions from his music career, but the singer accused of murdering teenager Celeste Rivas Hernandez is now relying on taxpayer-funded attorneys as his increasingly complicated criminal case moves toward trial.

And if you thought this situation couldn’t get any more bizarre, consider this: His defense team reportedly has approximately 40 terabytes of evidence to contend with.

That’s a whole lot of information. The singer, nee David Anthony Burke, appeared exhausted during his latest hearing. Correspondent Julia Deng described his puffy eyes, longer hair and unusually tired appearance. He’s stressed.

But the biggest issues seemed to revolve along the lines of money and lawyers. The once-promising musician has parted ways with his private attorneys. Now he’s represented by the Los Angeles County Public Defender’s Office.

According to testimony discussed during the proceedings, D4vd reportedly earned between $10 million and $11.5 million from 2023 through 2025. That. is a lot of money. On top of that, his recording agreement was also estimated to be worth as much as $19 million.

So how does somebody associated with that kind of money suddenly become unable to afford private legal representation? Last year had millions and today, nothing?

An attorney representing Celeste’s family has alleged that assets may have been concealed through corporate entities. They also want to know if the property or money was transferred to the singer’s mother.

However, these are questions. The allegations are disputed and unproven at press time. Some how they determined that D4vd qualified for representation after reviewing his financial circumstances. I do not know what they looked at.

Prosecutors are pushing for first-degree murder, continuous sexual abuse of a child under 14 and unlawful mutilation of human remains. He may end up on death row over these charges.

D4vd has pleaded not guilty.

The next hearing is scheduled for January 11, 2027, but a Law&Crime correspondent suggested the actual trial could be delayed even more because of the extensive evidence and changes in legal representation. I was thinking the trial may still come this year. That is apparently not happening.

Celeste’s fam has a reason for their inquiry on the money. They have a civil lawsuit pending.

Their civil attorney has raised the possibility that another person assisted in the alleged crimes or destruction of evidence. This is only an allegation as well. He acknowledged that the allegation was based on information and belief rather than established proof. I wonder if that person has money?

At any rate, no accomplice has been established.

For now, D4vd remains behind bars, his financial situation is dire and his legal future looks bleak.

And we are left with the rumors!
